P1● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

A man standing on the edge of a vertical cliff looks down at a boat. The angle between his line of sight and the vertical face of the cliff is 60°. The angle of depression of the boat is:

the angle of depression is measured from the horizontal, which is at 90° to the vertical (Topic 2). Why it applies: the angle given is measured from the wrong line, so it must be converted.

60° is measured from the vertical, not the horizontal.
90°−60°=30°90° - 60° = 30°90°−60°=30°.
90° is the angle between the vertical and the horizontal.
An angle of depression in these problems is always less than 90°.

Given: the angle between the line of sight and the vertical is 60°. Asked: the angle of depression.

Concept used: the angle of depression is measured from the horizontal, which is at 90° to the vertical (Topic 2). Why it applies: the angle given is measured from the wrong line, so it must be converted.

  1. 1

    The horizontal through his eye is at 90° to the vertical cliff.

  2. 2

    The line of sight lies between them, 60° from the vertical.

  3. 3

    So it is 90°−60°=30°90° - 60° = 30°90°−60°=30° below the horizontal: the angle of depression is 30°.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (b) ✔ 90°−60°=30°90° - 60° = 30°90°−60°=30°.
    • (a) ✘ 60° is measured from the vertical, not the horizontal.
    • (c) ✘ 90° is the angle between the vertical and the horizontal.
    • (d) ✘ An angle of depression in these problems is always less than 90°.

  4. Check: the angle of the right triangle at the man is 60° and the angle at the boat is the angle of depression; the two acute angles of a right triangle add up to 90°: 60°+30°=90°60° + 30° = 90°60°+30°=90° ✔.

  5. Answer (b)

    Common trap: Choosing (a): the 60° is between the line of sight and the cliff, not the horizontal.

height and ground distance → tan (Topic 3). Why it applies: the wall is vertical.

53≈8.665\sqrt{3} \approx 8.6653​≈8.66 m.

Concept used: height and ground distance → tan (Topic 3). Why it applies: the wall is vertical.

    h=153=1533=53h = \dfrac{15}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{15\sqrt{3}}{3} = 5\sqrt{3}h=3​15​=3153​​=53​.

P3● FoundationVery short answer · 1 markOriginal

A ladder 10 m long rests against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 60° with the level ground. How high up the wall does it reach?

Full solution

Given: ladder 10 m; angle with the ground 60°. Asked: the height h.

Concept used: height and slant length → sin (Topic 3). Why it applies: the ladder is the hypotenuse.

  1. 1

    sin⁡60°=h10\sin 60° = \dfrac{h}{10}sin60°=10h​, so 32=h10\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{h}{10}23​​=10h​.

  2. 2

    h=53h = 5\sqrt{3}h=53​.

  3. Check: the height is less than the ladder: 53≈8.66<105\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66 < 1053​≈8.66<10 ✔.

  4. Answer 535\sqrt{3}53​ m (about 8.66 m)

    Common trap: tan⁡60°=h10\tan 60° = \dfrac{h}{10}tan60°=10h​, giving 10310\sqrt{3}103​ m — taller than the ladder itself.

P4● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

A student whose eyes are 1.3 m above the ground stands 20 m from a tree. The angle of elevation of the top of the tree from her eyes is 45°. Find the height of the tree.

Full solution

Given: eye height 1.3 m; distance 20 m; angle 45°. Asked: the height of the tree.

Concept used: the triangle starts at the eye; add the eye height at the end (Topic 3). Why it applies: the angle is measured at her eyes.

  1. 1

    Part of the tree above her eyes: tan⁡45°=h20\tan 45° = \dfrac{h}{20}tan45°=20h​, so h=20h = 20h=20 m.

  2. 2

    Height of the tree =20+1.3=21.3= 20 + 1.3 = 21.3=20+1.3=21.3 m.

  3. Check: at 45° the part above the eye equals the horizontal distance (20 m) ✔; the tree is taller than that by her eye height ✔.

  4. Answer 21.3 m

    Common trap: Answering 20 m — the eye height forgotten.

P7● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

The angle of elevation of the top A of a tower from a point P on the level ground is 30°. The angle of depression of P from A is:

angle of depression at the top = angle of elevation at the ground point (alternate angles; Topic 2). Why it applies: the horizontal through A is parallel to the ground through P.

alternate angles are equal.
60° is the angle of the triangle at A, measured from the tower (the vertical).
90° is the angle at the foot of the tower.
This is 180°−30°180° - 30°180°−30°, the angle on the other side of the line of sight.

Given: angle of elevation of A from P is 30°. Asked: the angle of depression of P from A.

Concept used: angle of depression at the top = angle of elevation at the ground point (alternate angles; Topic 2). Why it applies: the horizontal through A is parallel to the ground through P.

  1. 1

    The horizontal through A and the ground are parallel; AP crosses both.

  2. 2

    The angle of depression at A and the angle of elevation at P are alternate angles, so they are equal: 30°.

    Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔ alternate angles are equal.
    • (b) ✘ 60° is the angle of the triangle at A, measured from the tower (the vertical).
    • (c) ✘ 90° is the angle at the foot of the tower.
    • (d) ✘ This is 180°−30°180° - 30°180°−30°, the angle on the other side of the line of sight.

  3. Check: draw the tower 10 m high with P 10310\sqrt{3}103​ m away: both angles have tan =13= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=3​1​ ✔.

  4. Answer (a)

    Common trap: (b) — measuring the angle at A from the vertical tower.
P8● FoundationTrue/False with justification · 1 markOriginal

True or false? Give a reason. "If the shadow of a vertical tower on level ground is longer than the tower, then the Sun's altitude is more than 45°."

Full solution

Given: shadow longer than the tower. Asked: true or false, with a reason.

Concept used: tan θ = tower ÷ shadow, and tan grows with the angle; tan⁡45°=1\tan 45° = 1tan45°=1 (Topics 1, 3). Why it applies: the altitude is the angle at the tip of the shadow.

  1. 1

    Shadow longer than the tower means towershadow<1\dfrac{\text{tower}}{\text{shadow}} < 1shadowtower​<1, so tan⁡θ<1=tan⁡45°\tan \theta < 1 = \tan 45°tanθ<1=tan45°.

  2. 2

    tan grows as the angle grows, so θ<45°\theta < 45°θ<45°.

  3. 3

    The statement says "more than 45°", so it is false.

  4. Check: example: a 10 m tower with a 10310\sqrt{3}103​ m shadow has altitude 30° (Practice question 6) — less than 45° ✔.

  5. Answer False. A shadow longer than the tower means the Sun's altitude is less than 45°.

    Common trap: Thinking "longer shadow, bigger angle". A lower Sun makes a longer shadow.

P9● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

The height of a building works out to 18(3+1)18(\sqrt{3} + 1)18(3​+1) m. (a) Write it to two decimal places, taking 3=1.732\sqrt{3} = 1.7323​=1.732. (b) Raju takes 3=1.7\sqrt{3} = 1.73​=1.7 and writes 48.6 m. By how much is he out?

Full solution

Given: the exact height 18(3+1)18(\sqrt{3} + 1)18(3​+1) m. Asked: the decimal; Raju's error.

Concept used: use the value of 3\sqrt{3}3​ the question gives, on the last line (Topic 1). Why it applies: rounding 3\sqrt{3}3​ early changes the answer.

  1. 1

    (a) 3+1=2.732\sqrt{3} + 1 = 2.7323​+1=2.732, and 18×2.732=49.17618 \times 2.732 = 49.17618×2.732=49.176, so the height is about 49.18 m.

  2. 2

    (b) 18×2.7=48.618 \times 2.7 = 48.618×2.7=48.6 m. Raju is out by 49.176−48.6=0.57649.176 - 48.6 = 0.57649.176−48.6=0.576 m, more than half a metre.

  3. Check: the error is 18×(1.732−1.7)=18×0.032=0.57618 \times (1.732 - 1.7) = 18 \times 0.032 = 0.57618×(1.732−1.7)=18×0.032=0.576 m ✔.

  4. Answer (a) about 49.18 m (b) by 0.576 m (too small)

    Common trap: Rounding 3\sqrt{3}3​ to 1.7 "to save time" — the error is multiplied by 18.

P10●● StandardShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

A kite string 80 m long is tied to a point O on the ground and makes an angle of 60° with the ground. Assuming no slack, find (a) the height of the kite (b) the distance from O to the point on the ground directly below the kite.

Full solution

Given: string 80 m; angle 60°. Asked: the height; the ground distance.

Concept used: height & slant → sin; ground distance & slant → cos (Topic 3). Why it applies: the string is the hypotenuse.

  1. 1

    (a) sin⁡60°=h80\sin 60° = \dfrac{h}{80}sin60°=80h​, so h=80×32=403h = 80 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 40\sqrt{3}h=80×23​​=403​ m.

  2. 2

    (b) cos⁡60°=d80\cos 60° = \dfrac{d}{80}cos60°=80d​, so d=80×12=40d = 80 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 40d=80×21​=40 m.

  3. Check: Pythagoras: (403)2+402=4800+1600=6400=802(40\sqrt{3})^2 + 40^2 = 4800 + 1600 = 6400 = 80^2(403​)2+402=4800+1600=6400=802 ✔.

  4. Answer (a) 40340\sqrt{3}403​ m (about 69.28 m) (b) 40 m

    Common trap: Using tan with the string: tan⁡60°=h80\tan 60° = \dfrac{h}{80}tan60°=80h​ gives 80380\sqrt{3}803​ m — higher than the string is long.

P11●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

A storm breaks a tree. The broken part bends over so that its top touches the ground 4 m from the foot of the tree, making an angle of 60° with the ground. Find the height of the tree before it broke. (Take 3=1.732\sqrt{3} = 1.7323​=1.732.)

Full solution

Given: the top lands 4 m from the foot; the broken part makes 60° with the ground. Asked: the original height.

Concept used: standing part from tan; broken (slant) part from cos; add (Topic 3). Why it applies: standing part, ground and broken part form one right triangle.

  1. 1

    Let the standing part be AB (B the foot), the broken part AC, BC=4BC = 4BC=4 m, ∠ACB=60°\angle ACB = 60°∠ACB=60°.

  2. 2

    Standing part: tan⁡60°=AB4\tan 60° = \dfrac{AB}{4}tan60°=4AB​, so AB=43AB = 4\sqrt{3}AB=43​.

  3. 3

    Broken part: cos⁡60°=4AC\cos 60° = \dfrac{4}{AC}cos60°=AC4​, so 12=4AC\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{4}{AC}21​=AC4​ and AC=8AC = 8AC=8.

  4. 4

    Height =AB+AC=43+8=4(2+3)= AB + AC = 4\sqrt{3} + 8 = 4(2 + \sqrt{3})=AB+AC=43​+8=4(2+3​).

  5. 5

    Decimal: 4×1.732=6.9284 \times 1.732 = 6.9284×1.732=6.928, so 6.928+8=14.9286.928 + 8 = 14.9286.928+8=14.928, about 14.93 m.

  6. Check: Pythagoras: AB2+BC2=48+16=64=AC2AB^2 + BC^2 = 48 + 16 = 64 = AC^2AB2+BC2=48+16=64=AC2 ✔.

  7. Answer 4(2+3)4(2 + \sqrt{3})4(2+3​) m, about 14.93 m

    Common trap: Using tan for the broken part, or giving only 434\sqrt{3}43​ m (the part still standing).

P12●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on level ground is 45°. After walking 24 m straight towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. Find the height of the tower. (Take 3=1.732\sqrt{3} = 1.7323​=1.732.)

Full solution

Given: angles 45° then 60°; walk 24 m. Asked: the height h.

Concept used: shared height; same side, so the far distance is x+24x + 24x+24 (Topic 4). Why it applies: both points are on one line with the foot.

  1. 1

    Let the near distance be x. From 60°: h=x3h = x\sqrt{3}h=x3​.

  2. 2

    From 45°: h=x+24h = x + 24h=x+24.

  3. 3

    So x3=x+24x\sqrt{3} = x + 24x3​=x+24, x(3−1)=24x(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 24x(3​−1)=24, and x=243−1=12(3+1)x = \dfrac{24}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = 12(\sqrt{3} + 1)x=3​−124​=12(3​+1).

  4. 4

    h=x+24=123+12+24=12(3+3)h = x + 24 = 12\sqrt{3} + 12 + 24 = 12(3 + \sqrt{3})h=x+24=123​+12+24=12(3+3​).

  5. 5

    Decimal: 12×4.732=56.78412 \times 4.732 = 56.78412×4.732=56.784, about 56.78 m.

  6. Check: h=x3=12(3+1)3=12(3+3)h = x\sqrt{3} = 12(\sqrt{3} + 1)\sqrt{3} = 12(3 + \sqrt{3})h=x3​=12(3​+1)3​=12(3+3​) ✔ — both triangles give the same height.

  7. Answer 12(3+3)12(3 + \sqrt{3})12(3+3​) m, about 56.78 m

    Common trap: tan⁡45°=h24\tan 45° = \dfrac{h}{24}tan45°=24h​ — using the walk as the whole distance.

P13●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

The shadow of a tower on level ground is 16 m longer when the Sun's altitude is 30° than when it is 45°. Find the height of the tower. (Take 3=1.732\sqrt{3} = 1.7323​=1.732.)

Full solution

Given: altitudes 30° and 45°; the difference of the shadows is 16 m. Asked: the height h.

Concept used: shared height; shadows h3h\sqrt{3}h3​ (30°) and hhh (45°); their difference is 16 m (Topic 4). Why it applies: both shadows start at the foot of the tower.

  1. 1

    h3−h=16h\sqrt{3} - h = 16h3​−h=16, so h(3−1)=16h(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 16h(3​−1)=16.

  2. 2

    h=163−1=16(3+1)2=8(3+1)h = \dfrac{16}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = \dfrac{16(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2} = 8(\sqrt{3} + 1)h=3​−116​=216(3​+1)​=8(3​+1).

  3. 3

    Decimal: 8×2.732=21.8568 \times 2.732 = 21.8568×2.732=21.856, about 21.86 m.

  4. Check: shadows 21.85621.85621.856 m (45°) and 21.856×1.732≈37.8621.856 \times 1.732 \approx 37.8621.856×1.732≈37.86 m (30°); difference about 16 m ✔.

  5. Answer 8(3+1)8(\sqrt{3} + 1)8(3​+1) m, about 21.86 m

    Common trap: Rationalising wrongly: 163−1=16(3+1)\dfrac{16}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = 16(\sqrt{3} + 1)3​−116​=16(3​+1) (forgetting to divide by 2) or 8(3−1)8(\sqrt{3} - 1)8(3​−1) (keeping the minus sign).

Given: tower 36 m; angles 30° and 45°; opposite sides. Asked: the distance between the men.

    Man at 30°: distance =363= 36\sqrt{3}=363​ m.

    Man at 45°: distance =36= 36=36 m.

    Distance between them =363+36=36(3+1)= 36\sqrt{3} + 36 = 36(\sqrt{3} + 1)=363​+36=36(3​+1).

  4. 4

    Decimal: 36×2.732=98.35236 \times 2.732 = 98.35236×2.732=98.352, about 98.35 m.

  6. Answer 36(3+1)36(\sqrt{3} + 1)36(3​+1) m, about 98.35 m

Concept used: alternate angles; shared height; the difference of the distances (Topic 4). Why it applies: both boats are on one line with the foot.

    Farther boat (30°): distance =903= 90\sqrt{3}=903​ m.

    Between them: 903−303=60390\sqrt{3} - 30\sqrt{3} = 60\sqrt{3}903​−303​=603​.

    Decimal: 60×1.732=103.9260 \times 1.732 = 103.9260×1.732=103.92 m.

P17●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

From the top of a house 21 m high, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 30° and the angle of depression of the foot of the tower is 60°. Find the height of the tower and the distance between the house and the tower.

Full solution

Given: house 21 m; elevation 30°; depression 60°. Asked: the height of the tower; the distance.

Concept used: depression → shared distance (alternate angles); elevation → part above the roof; tower = sum (Topic 5). Why it applies: the horizontal through the roof cuts the tower in two.

  1. 1

    Depression 60° to the foot: tan⁡60°=21d\tan 60° = \dfrac{21}{d}tan60°=d21​, so d=213=73d = \dfrac{21}{\sqrt{3}} = 7\sqrt{3}d=3​21​=73​ m.

  2. 2

    Elevation 30° to the top: part above the roof =dtan⁡30°=733=7= d \tan 30° = \dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = 7=dtan30°=3​73​​=7 m.

  3. 3

    Tower =7+21=28= 7 + 21 = 28=7+21=28 m.

    Speed =2439=833= \dfrac{24\sqrt{3}}{9} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{3}=9243​​=383​​ m per second.

P24●● StandardCase/source-based · 4 marksOriginal

Case: the water tank

A water tank stands on top of a vertical tower 16 m high. From a point P on the level ground, the angle of elevation of the bottom of the tank (the top of the tower) is 45°, and the angle of elevation of the top of the tank is 60°. (Take 3=1.732\sqrt{3} = 1.7323​=1.732.)

(ii) How high is the top of the tank above the ground? (1)

OR

Given: tower 16 m; angles 45° (bottom of the tank) and 60° (top of the tank). Asked: four answers.

Concept used: shared distance; differences of heights; then shared height for (iii)(B) (Topics 4, 5). Why it applies: everything is seen from one ground line.

  1. 1

    (i) tan⁡45°=16d\tan 45° = \dfrac{16}{d}tan45°=d16​, so d=16d = 16d=16 m.

  3. 3

    (iii)(A) Tank =163−16=16(3−1)= 16\sqrt{3} - 16 = 16(\sqrt{3} - 1)=163​−16=16(3​−1) m; 16×0.732=11.71216 \times 0.732 = 11.71216×0.732=11.712, about 11.71 m.

  4. 4

    (iii)(B) At 30°: distance =H3=163×3=48= H\sqrt{3} = 16\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 48=H3​=163​×3​=48 m. He walks 48−16=3248 - 16 = 3248−16=32 m.

  5. Check: (iii)(B) at 48 m, tan⁡(angle)=16348=33=13\tan(\text{angle}) = \dfrac{16\sqrt{3}}{48} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}tan(angle)=48163​​=33​​=3​1​ ✔.

  6. Answer (i) 16 m (ii) 16316\sqrt{3}163​ m, about 27.71 m (iii)(A) 16(3−1)16(\sqrt{3} - 1)16(3​−1) m, about 11.71 m (iii)(B) 32 m

    h(3+1)=723h(\sqrt{3} + 1) = 72\sqrt{3}h(3​+1)=723​, so h=7233+1=723(3−1)2=36(3−3)h = \dfrac{72\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3} + 1} = \dfrac{72\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} - 1)}{2} = 36(3 - \sqrt{3})h=3​+1723​​=2723​(3​−1)​=36(3−3​).

    Distances: h=36(3−3)h = 36(3 - \sqrt{3})h=36(3−3​) and 72−h=72−108+363=36(3−1)72 - h = 72 - 108 + 36\sqrt{3} = 36(\sqrt{3} - 1)72−h=72−108+363​=36(3​−1).

Full solution

Given: eye 9 m above the lake; elevation of the cloud 30°; depression of its reflection 60°. Asked: the height H of the cloud.

Concept used: the reflection is as far below the lake as the cloud is above it; two right triangles share the horizontal distance d (Topic 5). Why it applies: the cloud and its reflection are on one vertical line.

  1. 1

    The cloud is H−9H - 9H−9 m above the man's eye; its reflection is H+9H + 9H+9 m below his eye.

  2. 2

    Elevation 30°: tan⁡30°=H−9d\tan 30° = \dfrac{H - 9}{d}tan30°=dH−9​, so d=(H−9)3d = (H - 9)\sqrt{3}d=(H−9)3​.

  3. 3

    Depression 60°: tan⁡60°=H+9d\tan 60° = \dfrac{H + 9}{d}tan60°=dH+9​, so H+9=d3=3(H−9)H + 9 = d\sqrt{3} = 3(H - 9)H+9=d3​=3(H−9).

  4. 4

    H+9=3H−27H + 9 = 3H - 27H+9=3H−27, so 2H=362H = 362H=36 and H=18H = 18H=18 m.

  5. Check: d=93d = 9\sqrt{3}d=93​: 18−993=13=tan⁡30°\dfrac{18 - 9}{9\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \tan 30°93​18−9​=3​1​=tan30° ✔ and 18+993=33=3=tan⁡60°\dfrac{18 + 9}{9\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3} = \tan 60°93​18+9​=3​3​=3​=tan60° ✔.

  6. Answer 18 m

    Common trap: Taking the depression of the reflection to be equal to the elevation of the cloud. They are equal only if the eye is at the lake surface; here the eye is 9 m up.

From P he was 49.176+36=85.17649.176 + 36 = 85.17649.176+36=85.176 m away, and 49.176×1.732≈85.1749.176 \times 1.732 \approx 85.1749.176×1.732≈85.17 ✔.

P30●●● AdvancedProof · 3 marksOriginal

From two points on the same side of a tower of height h, in a straight line with its foot, at distances a and b from the foot (a>ba > ba>b), the angles of elevation of the top are 30° and 60°. (i) Show that h2=abh^2 = abh2=ab. (ii) Show that a=3ba = 3ba=3b. (iii) If b=10b = 10b=10 m, find h and a.

Given: distances a (30°) and b (60°). Asked: two results and the values.

Concept used: one ratio per triangle; multiply or divide the two equations (Topic 4). Why it applies: both triangles share h.

  1. 1

    Farther point (30°): tan⁡30°=ha\tan 30° = \dfrac{h}{a}tan30°=ah​, so h=a3h = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{3}}h=3​a​.

  2. 2

    Nearer point (60°): tan⁡60°=hb\tan 60° = \dfrac{h}{b}tan60°=bh​, so h=b3h = b\sqrt{3}h=b3​.

  3. 3

    (i) Multiply the two: h×h=a3×b3=abh \times h = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{3}} \times b\sqrt{3} = abh×h=3​a​×b3​=ab, so h2=abh^2 = abh2=ab.

  4. 4

    (ii) Set them equal: a3=b3\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{3}} = b\sqrt{3}3​a​=b3​, so a=3ba = 3ba=3b.

  5. 5

    (iii) b=10b = 10b=10: a=30a = 30a=30 m and h=b3=103h = b\sqrt{3} = 10\sqrt{3}h=b3​=103​ m; check (i): h2=300=30×10h^2 = 300 = 30 \times 10h2=300=30×10.

  6. Check: 10330=33=13=tan⁡30°\dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{30} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \tan 30°30103​​=33​​=3​1​=tan30° ✔ and 10310=3=tan⁡60°\dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{10} = \sqrt{3} = \tan 60°10103​​=3​=tan60° ✔.

  7. Answer (i), (ii) shown above (iii) h=103h = 10\sqrt{3}h=103​ m (about 17.32 m), a=30a = 30a=30 m

    Common trap: Choosing a and b freely in (iii). With these two angles the farther point is always exactly 3 times as far as the nearer one.

Given: pole 6 m; shadow 232\sqrt{3}23​ m. Asked: the Sun's elevation θ.

Concept used: tan θ = pole ÷ shadow (Topic 3). Why it applies: pole, shadow and sunray make a right triangle.

    tan⁡θ=623=33=3\tan \theta = \dfrac{6}{2\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}tanθ=23​6​=3​3​=3​, so θ=60°\theta = 60°θ=60°.

E2● FoundationTrue/False with justification · 1 markNCERT Exemplar Ch 8, Ex 8.2 Q7

Write 'True' or 'False' and justify your answer: If the length of the shadow of a tower is increasing, then the angle of elevation of the sun is also increasing.

Full solution

Given: the shadow is getting longer. Asked: true or false.

Concept used: tan θ = tower ÷ shadow; tan grows with the angle (Topics 1, 2). Why it applies: the tower's height stays the same.

  1. 1

    The tower's height is fixed. If the shadow gets longer, towershadow\dfrac{\text{tower}}{\text{shadow}}shadowtower​ gets smaller.

  2. 2

    A smaller tan means a smaller angle. So the angle of elevation of the Sun is decreasing.

  3. Check: 45° gives a shadow equal to the tower; 30° gives a shadow 3\sqrt{3}3​ times as long — a longer shadow for a smaller angle ✔.

  4. Answer False — a longer shadow means the Sun's angle of elevation is decreasing.

    Common trap: Thinking that "both increase together".

E3●● StandardTrue/False with justification · 1 markNCERT Exemplar Ch 8, Ex 8.2 Q8

Write 'True' or 'False' and justify your answer: If a man standing on a platform 3 metres above the surface of a lake observes a cloud and its reflection in the lake, then the angle of elevation of the cloud is equal to the angle of depression of its reflection.

Full solution

Given: eye 3 m above the lake. Asked: are the two angles equal?

Concept used: the reflection is as far below the lake as the cloud is above it (Practice question 26). Why it applies: the cloud and its reflection are on one vertical line, at the same horizontal distance d from the man.

  1. 1

    If the cloud is H m above the lake, it is H−3H - 3H−3 m above the man's eye, and its reflection is H+3H + 3H+3 m below his eye.

  2. 2

    tan⁡(elevation)=H−3d\tan(\text{elevation}) = \dfrac{H - 3}{d}tan(elevation)=dH−3​ and tan⁡(depression)=H+3d\tan(\text{depression}) = \dfrac{H + 3}{d}tan(depression)=dH+3​.

  3. 3

    H+3>H−3H + 3 > H - 3H+3>H−3, so the depression is bigger than the elevation: they are not equal.

  4. Check: with the numbers of Practice question 26 (eye 9 m up, cloud 18 m), the two angles are 30° and 60° — not equal ✔.

  5. Answer False — the angle of depression of the reflection is greater.

    Common trap: Treating the man's eye as if it were on the lake surface.

E4● FoundationTrue/False with justification · 1 markNCERT Exemplar Ch 8, Ex 8.2 Q11

Write 'True' or 'False' and justify your answer: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 30°. If the height of the tower is doubled, then the angle of elevation of its top will also be doubled.

Full solution

Given: angle 30°; height doubled, distance unchanged. Asked: true or false.

Concept used: tan θ = height ÷ distance (Topic 3). Why it applies: the observer stays at the same distance.

  1. 1

    At first tan⁡30°=hd=13\tan 30° = \dfrac{h}{d} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}tan30°=dh​=3​1​.

  2. 2

    With height 2h2h2h: tan⁡θ=2hd=23≈1.15\tan \theta = \dfrac{2h}{d} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.15tanθ=d2h​=3​2​≈1.15.

  3. 3

    A doubled angle would be 60°, with tan⁡60°=3≈1.73\tan 60° = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73tan60°=3​≈1.73. Since 1.15≠1.731.15 \ne 1.731.15=1.73, the angle is not doubled.

  4. Check: to reach 60° the height would have to become 3×3=3\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 33​×3​=3 times the first height (tan⁡60°=3tan⁡30°\tan 60° = 3\tan 30°tan60°=3tan30°) — not 2 times ✔.

  5. Answer False

    Common trap: Thinking that angles grow in step with heights.

E5● FoundationTrue/False with justification · 1 markNCERT Exemplar Ch 8, Ex 8.2 Q12

Write 'True' or 'False' and justify your answer: If the height of a tower and the distance of the point of observation from its foot, both, are increased by 10%, then the angle of elevation of its top remains unchanged.

Full solution

Given: both lengths × 1.1. Asked: true or false.

Concept used: tan θ depends only on height ÷ distance (Practice question 23). Why it applies: the ratio does not change.

  1. 1

    New ratio: 1.1h1.1d=hd\dfrac{1.1h}{1.1d} = \dfrac{h}{d}1.1d1.1h​=dh​ — the same tan, so the same angle.

  2. Check: a 10 m tower seen from 10 m (45°) becomes 11 m seen from 11 m — still 45° ✔.

  3. Answer True

    Common trap: Thinking that "a taller tower always looks steeper" — only if the distance stays the same.

A ladder 15 metres long just reaches the top of a vertical wall. If the ladder makes an angle of 60° with the wall, find the height of the wall.

Full solution

Given: ladder 15 m; angle with the wall 60°. Asked: the height of the wall.

Concept used: the angle with the ground is 90°−60°=30°90° - 60° = 30°90°−60°=30°; height & ladder → sin (Topic 3). Why it applies: the wall is vertical, so the two acute angles of the right triangle add up to 90°.

    Angle between the ladder and the ground: 90°−60°=30°90° - 60° = 30°90°−60°=30°.

    sin⁡30°=h15\sin 30° = \dfrac{h}{15}sin30°=15h​, so h=152=7.5h = \dfrac{15}{2} = 7.5h=215​=7.5 m.

  4. Answer 152\dfrac{15}{2}215​ m, that is 7.5 m

    Common trap: Using 60° as the angle with the ground: 15sin⁡60°=153215\sin 60° = \dfrac{15\sqrt{3}}{2}15sin60°=2153​​ m.

    H=d3=5(3+1)3=5(3+3)H = d\sqrt{3} = 5(\sqrt{3} + 1)\sqrt{3} = 5(3 + \sqrt{3})H=d3​=5(3​+1)3​=5(3+3​).

Full solution

Given: windows at 2 m and 6 m; angles 60° (lower) and 30° (upper). Asked: the balloon's height H.

Concept used: shared horizontal distance d (Topic 5). Why it applies: both windows are on one vertical line, the same distance from the balloon.

  1. 1

    Lower window: tan⁡60°=H−2d\tan 60° = \dfrac{H - 2}{d}tan60°=dH−2​, so H−2=d3H - 2 = d\sqrt{3}H−2=d3​.

  2. 2

  3. 3

    Subtract: 4=d3−d3=2d34 = d\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{d}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2d}{\sqrt{3}}4=d3​−3​d​=3​2d​, so d=23d = 2\sqrt{3}d=23​.

  4. 4

    H=2+23×3=2+6=8H = 2 + 2\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 2 + 6 = 8H=2+23​×3​=2+6=8 m.

  5. Check: from the upper window: 8−623=13=tan⁡30°\dfrac{8 - 6}{2\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \tan 30°23​8−6​=3​1​=tan30° ✔.

  6. Answer 8 m

    Common trap: Measuring both heights from the ground (tan⁡60°=Hd\tan 60° = \dfrac{H}{d}tan60°=dH​): the angles are measured at the windows.

C1 — Case: India Gate● FoundationCase/source-based · 5 marksCBSE Mathematics Class X Case Study Question Bank, Some Application of Trigonometry, Case Study 1

(Picture, described: a photograph of India Gate, the stone arch, seen from the road in front of it.)

A group of students of class X visited India Gate on an education trip. The teacher and students had interest in history as well. The teacher narrated that India Gate, official name Delhi Memorial, originally called All-India War Memorial, monumental sandstone arch in New Delhi, dedicated to the troops of British India who died in wars fought between 1914 and 1919.The teacher also said that India Gate, which is located at the eastern end of the Rajpath (formerly called the Kingsway), is about 138 feet (42 metres) in height.

  1. What is the angle of elevation if they are standing at a distance of 42m away from the monument?

a) 30° b) 45° c) 60° d) 0°

  1. They want to see the tower at an angle of 60°. So, they want to know the distance where they should stand and hence find the distance.

a) 25.24 m b) 20.12 m c) 42 m d) 24.64 m

  1. If the altitude of the Sun is at 60°, then the height of the vertical tower that will cast a shadow of length 20 m is

a) 20320\sqrt{3}203​ m b) 203\dfrac{20}{\sqrt{3}}3​20​ m c) 153\dfrac{15}{\sqrt{3}}3​15​ m d) 15315\sqrt{3}153​ m

  1. The ratio of the length of a rod and its shadow is 1:1 . The angle of elevation of the Sun is

a) 30° b) 45° c) 60° d) 90°

  1. The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when the object viewd is below the horizontal level is

a) corresponding angle b) angle of elevation c) angle of depression d) complete angle

(Notes on the bank's key: the key gives 1. b), 2. a) 25.24 m, 3. a), 4. b), 5. a) "corresponding angle". Part 2: the exact distance is 423=143≈24.25\dfrac{42}{\sqrt{3}} = 14\sqrt{3} \approx 24.253​42​=143​≈24.25 m — none of the four options is correct (25.24 m looks like 24.25 m with two digits swapped). Part 5: the correct answer is c) angle of depression; the key's a) is a slip. The case, like the bank, ignores the height of the students' eyes.)

Full solution

Given: height 42 m. Asked: five answers.

Concept used: tan of the angle of elevation; the definitions (Topics 2, 3). Why it applies: each part is one right triangle or one definition.

  1. 1

    Part 1: tan⁡θ=4242=1\tan \theta = \dfrac{42}{42} = 1tanθ=4242​=1, so θ=45°\theta = 45°θ=45° → b).

  2. 2

    Part 2: tan⁡60°=42x\tan 60° = \dfrac{42}{x}tan60°=x42​, so x=423=143≈24.25x = \dfrac{42}{\sqrt{3}} = 14\sqrt{3} \approx 24.25x=3​42​=143​≈24.25 m — not among the options (the bank keys a) 25.24 m).

  3. 3

    Part 3: tan⁡60°=h20\tan 60° = \dfrac{h}{20}tan60°=20h​, so h=203h = 20\sqrt{3}h=203​ m → a).

  4. 4

    Part 4: tan⁡θ=11=1\tan \theta = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1tanθ=11​=1, so θ=45°\theta = 45°θ=45° → b).

  5. 5

    Part 5: below the horizontal → c) angle of depression.

  6. Check: part 2: 143×3=4214\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 42143​×3​=42 ✔, and 14×1.732=24.24814 \times 1.732 = 24.24814×1.732=24.248.

  7. Answer

    1. b) 45° 2. 14314\sqrt{3}143​ m ≈ 24.25 m (no option fits; the bank keys a) 25.24 m) 3. a) 20320\sqrt{3}203​ m 4. b) 45° 5. c) angle of depression (the bank keys a))

    Common trap: Part 3: dividing by 3\sqrt{3}3​ instead of multiplying. A 60° Sun gives a shadow shorter than the tower, so the tower is longer than 20 m.
